source.title: FPT Suspects and Tough Customers: Open Problems of Downey and Fellows

accepted.question_text: Given an undirected graph G and another graph H as the parameter, is H topologically contained in G, meaning that some subdivision of H appears as a subgraph of G?

evidence.quote:
Topological Containment FPT
Instance: An undirected graphG
Parameter: Ag r a p hH
Question: Is H topologically contained inG?

evidence.quote:

Instance: An undirected graphG
Parameter: Ag r a p hH
Question: Does H h a sa ni m m e r s i o ni nG?

accepted.question_text: Given a directed graph G and a positive integer k, is there a set S of k vertices such that every directed cycle of G contains at least one vertex of S?

evidence.quote:
Directed Feedback Vertex Set FPT
Instance: A directed graphG
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is there a setS of k vertices such that each directed cycle ofG
contains a member ofS?

accepted.question_text: Is there a single-exponential fixed-parameter algorithm for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on planar directed graphs, where the parameter is the size k of the feedback vertex set?
accepted.context_brief: Planar directed feedback vertex set algorithms

evidence.quote:
It remains open if there exist a single exponential algorithm forDirected Feedback Vertex
Set even on planar graphs.

accepted.question_text: Does Directed Feedback Vertex Set admit a polynomial kernel when parameterized by the size k of the feedback vertex set?
accepted.context_brief: Kernelization for directed feedback vertex set

evidence.quote: The existence of polynomial kernel is also open.

accepted.question_text: Given a directed planar graph G and k ordered pairs of vertices ⟨r1, s1⟩, ..., ⟨rk, sk⟩, does G contain k pairwise vertex-disjoint directed paths P1, ..., Pk such that Pi runs from ri to si for each i?
accepted.context_brief: Directed disjoint paths in planar digraphs

evidence.quote:
Planar Directed Disjoint Paths Open
Instance: A directed planar graph G and k pairs ⟨r1,s 1⟩,..., ⟨rk,s k⟩ of
vertices ofG
Parameter: k
Question: Does G have k vertex-disjoint pathsP1,...,P k with Pi running
from ri to si?
The problemis open.

accepted.question_text: Given a weighted undirected planar graph G with terminals {x1, ..., xk} and a positive integer M, is there a set of edges of total weight at most M whose removal separates every terminal from every other terminal?

evidence.quote:
Planar Multiway Cut W[1]-hard
Instance: A weighted undirected planar graph G with terminals
{x1,...,x k} and a positive integerM
Parameter: k
Question: Is there a set of edges of total weight≤ M whose removal
disconnects each terminal from all others?

The problem was shown to be W[1]-hard in
2011 [34].

accepted.question_text: Given k sequences Xi over a fixed alphabet Σ and a positive integer m, is there a string X in Σ* of length m that is a subsequence of every Xi?

integer m
Parameter: k
Question: Is there a stringX ∈Σ∗of lengthm that is a subsequence of
each of theXi?

accepted.question_text: Given an undirected graph G and a positive integer k, is the crossing number of G at most k, where the crossing number is the minimum number of edge crossings in a planar drawing of G?

evidence.quote:
Crossing Number FPT

Question: Is the crossing number ofG is at mostk?

accepted.question_text: Given an undirected graph G and positive integers k and d, can the vertex set V(G) be partitioned into disjoint subsets V1, ..., Vm such that each part Vi has size at most k and at most d edges have exactly one endpoint in Vi?

evidence.quote:
Minimum Degree Graph Partition FPT
Instance: An undirected graphG
Parameter: Positive integersk and d
Question: Can V(G) be partitioned into disjoint subsetsV1,...,V m so
that for 1≤i ≤m, |Vi|≤ k and at mostd edges have exactly one endpoint
in Vi?

accepted.question_text: Given a graph G, an integer S, and an edge-weight function w: E(G) → Z, is there a tour through at least k vertices of G whose total cost is at most S?

evidence.quote:
Short Cheap Tour FPT
Instance: Ag r a p hG, integerS, and edge weightingw:E(G) → Z
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is there a tour through at leastk nodes of G of cost at most
S?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a k-polymatroid, meaning a polymatroid ρ: 2^E → Z with ρ(e) ≤ k for every element e of the ground set E. Is M hypergraphic; that is, does there exist a hypergraph H on edge set E such that M is the hypergraphic polymatroid χ_H defined by χ_H(A) = |A| − κ(H|A) for every A ⊆ E, where A is the set of vertices contained in the hyperedge set A and κ(H|A) is the number of connected components of the restriction of H to A?

evidence.quote:
Polymatroid Recognition Open
Instance: A k-polymatroid M
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is M hypergraphic?

A k-polymatroid is a polymatroid with ρ(e) ≤ k for every e ∈E. Given a
hypergraph H with vertex setV and edge setE, the hypergraphic polymatroid
of H is a functionχH :2 E → Z deﬁned by
χH(A)= |
A|−κ(H|A),

accepted.question_text: Given finite posets P and Q, is P a chain minor of Q? Here P is a chain minor of Q if there exists a partial mapping ρ from elements of Q to elements of P such that for every chain C in P there is a chain C′ in Q for which the restriction of ρ to C′ is an isomorphism of chains from C′ to C.

evidence.quote:
Chain Minor Ordering Open
Instance: A ﬁnite posetQ
Parameter: A ﬁnite posetP
Question: Is P a chain minor ofQ?

We say thatP =( V,<)isachainminor P′ =( V′,<)if thereisapartialmapping
ρ: V′ → V with the following property: for every chainC of P, there is a chain
C′ of P′ such thatρrestricted toC′ is an isomorphism of chains fromC′ to C.

accepted.question_text: In Generalized Hex played on an undirected graph G with distinguished vertices v1 and v2, two players alternately place white and black pebbles on previously unoccupied vertices, player one moving first and winning if the white vertices contain a path from v1 to v2. Given G, v1, v2, and a positive integer k, does player one have a winning strategy that succeeds within at most k of player one's moves?
accepted.context_brief: Parameterized game strategies in generalized Hex

evidence.quote:
Short Generalized Hex Open
Instance: An undirected graphG with two distinguished verticesv1 and
v2
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Does player one have a winning strategy of at mostk moves in
Generalized Hex?

Player one starts
by placing a white pebble on a vertexofG. Then alternately playersmakemoves,
at each move a pebble is placed on an occupied vertex. Player one wins if he can
construct a path of white vertices fromv1 to v2.

accepted.question_text: Given a finite poset P, is the jump number of P at most k, where the jump number is the minimum possible number of consecutive incomparable pairs in a linear extension of P?

evidence.quote:
Jump Number FPT
Instance: Ap o s e tP
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is the jump number ofP at mostk?

The jump number ofP is the minimum number of jumps inL, where minimum
is taken over all the linear extensionsL of P.

accepted.question_text: Given two families of multivariate polynomials p1, ..., pk and q1, ..., qk, each represented by listing all monomials with nonzero coefficients and with no a priori bound on the number of variables or on the degrees, can one decide in deterministic fixed-parameter tractable time, parameterized by k, whether the identity ∏_{i=1}^k p_i = ∏_{i=1}^k q_i holds?

accepted.question_text: Given a basis X = {x1, x2, ..., xn} ⊂ Z^n for a lattice L and a positive integer k, is there a nonzero lattice vector x in L whose Euclidean norm ||x||_2 is at most k?

evidence.quote:
Shortest Vector Open
Instance: Ab a s i sX = {x1,x 2,...,x n}⊂ Zn for a latticeL
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is there a non-zero vectorx ∈L, such that∥x∥2 ≤k?

accepted.question_text: Given a red-blue bipartite graph G = (R, B, E) and a positive integer k, is there a nonempty subset R′ of the red side R with at most k vertices such that every vertex in B has an even number of neighbors in R′? Equivalently, is there a nonzero vector x over GF(2) with at most k nonzero coordinates satisfying A x = 0 for the corresponding binary matrix representation?

evidence.quote:
Even Set Open
Instance: An undirected red/blue bipartite graphG =( R,B,E)
Parameter: A positive integerk
Question: Is there a non-empty set of at mostk vertices R ⊆R, such that
each member ofB has an even number of neighbors inR?

– Given a matrixA over the two-element ﬁeldGF[2], is there a nonzero vector
x having at mostk nonzero coordinates and satisfyingAx =0 ?
